content: {"summary":"Two waves of AUTH‑E401X errors occurred because the July 2026 release changed the session encoding in redis‑sessions. New pods could not read sessions written by old pods and old pods could not read sessions written by the new version, so each direction of incompatibility produced a wave of logout errors.","likely_cause":"Incompatible session encoding between old and new auth‑service versions caused unreadable sessions in both directions.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The release changed session encoding, making new pods unable to read old sessions and vice‑versa.","evidence_ids":["RB-026#4"],"quote":"New pods couldn't decode sessions written by old pods, and the reverse."},{"text":"First wave occurred at 14:08 when the first new pod became Ready, causing AUTH‑E401X spikes.","evidence_ids":["RB-026#4"],"quote":"At 14:08, as the first new pod became Ready, `AUTH-E401X` jumped."},{"text":"Second wave happened after rollback when old pods resumed, affecting sessions created during the release.","evidence_ids":["INC-0178#1"],"quote":"The second wave came from sessions created while the release was serving."}],"next_checks":["Verify that future releases include a forward‑compatible session reader before changing the writer","Monitor AUTH‑E401X error rates per ReplicaSet during rollouts to detect version‑specific spikes","Confirm Redis primary and session data remain healthy during deployments","Review rollout procedure to ensure old pods are not serving traffic while new pods cannot read existing sessions"]}
